prepared.title: Choose a model for workshop registrations
prepared.teaching: Select cardinalities, status ownership and relationship/entity representation. Both intended alternatives can pass.

prepared.title: Build a query tree
prepared.teaching: Construct a join/filter/projection tree. Inspect intermediate tables; matching finite instances is not an equivalence proof.

prepared.title: Rewrite a query tree
prepared.teaching: Push filters down using checked rules. Explain each side condition; fewer intermediate cells are a teaching metric.

prepared.title: Few matches: scan or index?
prepared.teaching: Compare the supplied cost formulas: 5,210 teaching units for the index versus 20,000 for a scan.

prepared.title: Many matches: scan or index?
prepared.teaching: A broad predicate can make an index worse. Keep the query fixed and compare the root cost.

prepared.title: Choose a join order
prepared.teaching: Choose access paths, join order and methods for a library query. Duplicate loan results are meaningful.

prepared.title: Plan with less hash memory
prepared.teaching: Choose the hash build side and obey each operator's memory bound. A previously attractive plan may become illegal.

prepared.title: Follow a lookup path
prepared.teaching: Follow separators to the correct leaf and identify the entry. Leaves store data; internal keys route the search.

prepared.title: Scan a key interval
prepared.teaching: Start at the lower-bound leaf, then follow leaf links. Include exactly the required keys and pages.

prepared.title: Insert and split a leaf
prepared.teaching: Preserve sorted entries, leaf links and separator meaning. Different legal repairs are accepted.

prepared.title: Delete and repair underflow
prepared.teaching: Inspect occupancy. Borrow or merge as needed, and update the parent separators.

prepared.title: Propagate a split
prepared.teaching: Carry a split into an internal page and possibly a new root; preserve existing page identities.

prepared.title: Shrink the root
prepared.teaching: A root with one child is removed. The new root must still describe the complete leaf order.

prepared.title: Derive an attribute closure
prepared.teaching: Apply an FD only when every left-hand attribute is known. Continue to a fixed point.

prepared.title: Practice a closure with feedback
prepared.teaching: This activity gives practice feedback and no points. Use it before the scored reasoning examples.

prepared.title: Find one candidate key
prepared.teaching: A key must determine every attribute and be minimal by inclusion.

prepared.title: Find all candidate keys
prepared.teaching: Completeness matters as well as validity: an omitted key makes an all-keys answer incomplete.

prepared.title: Prove an implied dependency
prepared.teaching: Give a productive derivation. A claim of implication without its required evidence is incomplete.

prepared.title: Refute a dependency
prepared.teaching: Construct two rows satisfying every given FD while agreeing on the proposed determinant and disagreeing on its dependent.

prepared.title: Compare candidate-key sizes
prepared.teaching: Minimal does not mean minimum cardinality. Candidate keys of different sizes may coexist.

prepared.title: Can an empty key work?
prepared.teaching: An empty determinant can determine all attributes under the stated FDs; do not silently assume keys must be nonempty.

prepared.title: Decompose while keeping registrations
prepared.teaching: Keep the student/course link. Attribute coverage and dependency preservation alone do not prove losslessness.

prepared.title: Classify a relation
prepared.teaching: Find the highest normal form and a violating dependency for the next one. Assume atomic values.

prepared.title: Compare losslessness and FD preservation
prepared.teaching: A lossless BCNF decomposition can fail to preserve an FD. Examine the chase and counterexample rather than only the label.

prepared.title: Two increments, one counter
prepared.teaching: Predict 110, inspect remembered reads, explain the cycle, then repair to a legal acyclic schedule. The serial result is 120.

prepared.title: Independent transactions
prepared.teaching: Operations on different objects do not create conflicts. Include isolated transactions in a serial certificate.

prepared.title: Shared reads
prepared.teaching: Reading the same object twice does not create a conflict. Avoid adding an edge just because the object is shared.

prepared.title: Competing writes
prepared.teaching: Write/write pairs can conflict. Explain the earlier/later operation witness for each directed edge.

prepared.title: Direct edges and a chain
prepared.teaching: Distinguish direct conflict edges from reachability. A transitive path is not an extra direct witness.

prepared.title: A blind-write limitation
prepared.teaching: Conflict serializability is sufficient, not necessary for view serializability. A matching final value does not prove the conflict graph acyclic.
